issues: Rationale misdescribes the delivered candidate's authoritative evidence. The CONTROL HISTORY section claims '21 outcomes met ... The single unmet control is hmm-reformat-valid' and the LIMITATIONS section claims the LuxC.hmm representation latitude is 'not yet [corroborated] by a passing control, pending the corrected probe script'. The fresh control_summary for this candidate (sha256 cb170f7e...) reports expected_outcomes_met = 22, and the hmm-reformat-valid record itself shows all seven checks passing (probe executed, probe_valid_execution true, submission_after_probe LuxC.hmm sha256 93d8d381..., report passed = true). The stale counts are attributable to the supplied author_input_control_summary (21/22), which the author may quote without predicting later execution, but the delivered rationale must describe the current, authoritative execution state, not a superseded one.

False technical account of the delivered grader's continuation handling. Rationale item (3) asserts the probe's two trailing backslashes, after continuation joining, leave a stray backslash token (6 tokens) that the grader correctly rejects as a malformed STATS line, and that the intended alternative passes only with 'unchanged grader code' and a corrected single-backslash script. In the delivered _logical_lines, a line ending in one or two backslashes is a continuation and a doubled trailing backslash is collapsed (body = body[:-1].rstrip() when the remaining text still ends in a backslash), so the split 'STATS  LOCAL  FORWARD' line joins to a valid 5-token 'STATS LOCAL FORWARD -5.7663 +0.69925' line and passes - exactly what the fresh control shows. Since the mutation script is byte-identical between initial_probes and probes, the earlier failure and the current pass cannot both be explained by 'unchanged continuation/STATS rules': either the continuation/STATS parsing of the candidate actually changed relative to the earlier candidate hash (contradicting the explicit claims 'I did NOT alter the continuation/STATS rules' and 'unchanged grader code'), or the earlier failure was misdiagnosed. The revision must disclose the actual behavioral diff between candidate versions and stop asserting the continuation logic is unchanged. Note: the change only widens acceptance of a documented representation variant and does not let any wrong_solution probe pass (all 13 still fail as intended), so this is a disclosure defect, not a science defect.

Public contract does not state the relative-tolerance denominator. num_close(..., relative=True) uses max(|reference|, |submitted|) as the denominator for E-value comparisons; the public addendum says only 'relative tolerance 0.02'. The executed x1.05 perturbations exceed 0.02 under either interpretation, so no executed outcome is affected, but the public rule should name the denominator convention so what is accepted is fully determined. Cosmetic contract clarification only; no outcome change required.

Independence provenance wording. The tolerance basis cites 'independent recomputations' / 'two independent programs', but both the oracle and the independently executed comparison program drive the same pyhmmer 0.12.3 / HMMER 3.4 C engine. The tolerances are independently justified by the formats' print precision, and the rationale's limitations correctly disclaim cross-version portability, but 'independent' should be qualified (independent programs, shared engine) wherever it appears in the contract's tolerance section.

Documentation-level observation, no outcome change required: non-numeric junk tokens appended to insert/transition rows are silently ignored as annotations (only their absence from the reference value counts fails), which is documented latitude and cannot admit a wrong scientific result since every numeric or '*' token is still aligned with the reference; consider stating this acceptance more explicitly, as the rationale's own limitations section already half-acknowledges it.
rationale: The executed grader is scientifically sound: complete endpoint coverage (both terminal artifacts fully compared), contract wording matches the code check by check, tolerance-boundary and wrong-solution probes fail on substantive comparisons, all expected values are read from the reference at grading time, and the fresh 22-control suite on this candidate hash (cb170f7e...) met every intended outcome, including the previously failing hmm-reformat-valid. However, the candidate's own rationale misdescribes the delivered artifact and its fresh evidence: it claims 21/22 controls with hmm-reformat-valid unmet and asserts the delivered grader rejects the probe's two-backslash STATS continuation as a 6-token malformed line, when the delivered _logical_lines collapses doubled trailing backslashes and the fresh record shows that exact, unchanged mutation script passing all checks. Because probe scripts are byte-identical between initial_probes and probes, the outcome flip is only explainable by an undisclosed change to the grader's continuation handling between candidate versions (contradicting 'I did NOT alter the continuation/STATS rules'/'unchanged grader code') or by a misdiagnosed earlier failure; the rationale as delivered is not a reliable account of the diff between candidates. This is an accuracy/disclosure defect, not a science defect: no acceptance rule was weakened for wrong science (all 13 wrong_solution probes still fail on resolved substantive comparisons), no coverage was removed, and the public contract itself accurately describes the current code's behavior. Required revision: a corrected rationale/annotation layer that (a) states the authoritative fresh control state (22/22, hmm-reformat-valid passing), (b) reconciles or discloses the actual grader-code difference on continuation handling between candidate hashes, and (c) optionally clarifies the E-value denominator convention and the shared pyhmmer engine behind the 'independent programs' wording. If any grader code changes, all controls and this review must be repeated on the new candidate; the current evidence stays attached to hash cb170f7e...

source_coverage.rationale: Audited against the original converted source (inputs/original.py, trial/source.diff), the preparation plan (inputs/plan.json) and the export code (inputs/exports.py). The source has exactly two terminal scientific products: the Plan7 profile HMM written by hmm.write (LuxC.hmm) and the domain hits table written by hits.write(format='domains') (LuxC.domtbl). Both are preserved and fully compared: the HMM header (name, alphabet/order, LENG, NSEQ, EFFN, CKSUM, all STATS LOCAL parameters), every match/insert emission and transition value including the COMPO group and '*' zero-probability tokens, and every domtbl target block and domain row (identities, counts, coordinates, E-values, scores, biases, accuracy, descriptions), plus cross-file relations. The two excluded items are correctly excluded diagnostic displays, not terminal scientific results: hmm.consensus (notebook narrative: 'We can have a look at the consensus sequence' - a non-assigned inspection whose content is represented inside the saved HMM) and the printed single top-hit alignment ali (narrative: 'We can then query the TopHits object' - a demonstrative display of one hit's TopHits contents; its reported quantities lie in LuxC.domtbl). pyhmmer.__version__ is incidental display, not an endpoint. No missing endpoints in the original source and no omissions from the preparation inventory; the materialization mirrors both terminal artifacts into the reference directory as full copies, so permitted-supplied-intermediate policy is not implicated. No supplied artifact replaces or removes a required endpoint, and no scientific scope change was made relative to the source. The DATE/COM provenance lines remain correctly outside comparison.
remaining_validation: Cross-engine reproducibility is untested: the reference, the recomputed run and the independently executed comparison control all drive the same pyhmmer 0.12.3 / HMMER 3.4 C engine, so engine-level independence of the tolerance basis is established only via serialization precision plus the byte-identical domtbl observations, not via a second engine.

The delivered rationale's account of the continuation/STATS parsing and of the hmm-reformat-valid control history does not match the fresh records and must be reconciled/expanded per the overall review issues, though the underlying comparison scope itself is unaffected.
